title: Sound, Light and Heat Energy
seo_title: Primary 2 Basic Science: Sound, Light and Heat Energy Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: Primary 2 Basic Science: You and Energy
standard_text: Sound, light and heat are forms of energy. Sound is made by vibrations; light travels in straight lines and can be reflected; heat moves from hotter to cooler objects. (summary of the Basic Science curriculum, Primary 2, theme: You and Energy)
meta_desc: Free Primary 2 Basic Science worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: You and Energy): vibrations and sound, pitch and loudness, sources of light, materials and light, and heat. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Sound, light and heat are forms of energy.
key_sub: Heat moves from hot things to cold things.
body_html:
How to think about it

Sound is made when objects vibrate; it travels through air, liquids and solids. Pitch is how high or low a sound is; loudness is how strong it is.

Light travels in straight lines from a source; it passes through transparent materials and is blocked by opaque ones. Heat moves from a hotter object to a cooler one: a spoon in hot soup gets hot.

Example

Why does a metal spoon in hot soup get hot?

Heat moves.

Answer: heat moves from the soup to the spoon

Example

Which material lets light through?

Clear

Answer: clear glass

Common mistakes

  • Thinking cold moves into things.
  • Mixing up pitch and loudness.
  • Thinking light bends around corners.

faq.q: Why are pot handles made of wood or plastic?
faq.a: They do not conduct heat well, so they stay cool to hold.

faq.q: Why do we see lightning before we hear thunder?
faq.a: Light travels much faster than sound.

items.q: How could you make a guitar note higher?

items.q: What happens to the pitch when a guitar string is made shorter?

items.q: Which is an artificial source of light?
items.e: People make artificial sources.

items.q: In a room with no light at all, could you see a silver spoon?
c: No. With no light, no light can reflect from it into your eyes.
Yes, if you wait for your eyes to get used to it.
Yes, if it is shiny or white.
Yes, a little, because objects glow.
items.e: We see objects when light reflects off them into our eyes. Dark is the absence of light.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a light source: a campfire, a cat's eye reflector on a road, a firefly or a star?

items.e: A cat's eye reflector on a road does not make its own light; it reflects light.

items.q: Is a torch that is switched on a light source?

items.e: Sources give out light; everything else is seen because it reflects light.

items.q: Dayo compares two things. Which has more total thermal energy: a bathtub of warm water (40 °C) or a cup of hot tea (80 °C)?
c: They have the same thermal energy.
items.e: Thermal energy is the total energy of all the particles; the larger amount has far more particles.

items.q: A hot pan touches the cold water poured into it. In which direction does heat flow?
c: from the cold water poured into it to a hot pan
from a hot pan to the cold water poured into it
items.e: Heat flows from a hotter object to a colder one.

items.q: Ice touches the warm drink in a glass. Which one loses heat?
c: the warm drink in a glass
items.e: The hotter object loses heat to the colder one.

items.q: An ice cube touches your hand. Which one gains heat?
items.e: The colder object gains heat from the hotter one.
